transcriptionDecisions: Mozart: agree with supplied bars 1–4, including G-D-G-B in bar 2 and C-A-F#-A in bar 4. All five string desks follow the line in unison/octaves; cello/bass are an octave below the lead. 132 rather than 138 bpm permits an 8-second clip with the bar-4 rest and a short release.

Swan Lake: agree that the opening is F#5 dropping to B4. At quarter=66 the complete requested contour exceeds 10 seconds; the delivered perfect stops at the held F#5 after the first two bars. It contains eight melody attacks, so there are no ninth–twelfth notes to report. Full corrected contour is retained in excerpts.py.
Vivaldi: agree with the supplied pitch contour and implement the soft echo. The excerpt ends on B4, a ritornello phrase division on the dominant, rather than inventing a tonic cadence.

Chopin: agree with Bb4–G5–F5–G5–F5–Eb5–Bb4, then G5–C5–C6–G5–Bb5–Ab5; remove the erroneous Eb-D-Eb-F passage. F-G-F uses eighth notes within the 12/8 bar. The 9-second excerpt ends at the opening two-bar boundary on Ab5, before the next G5; this is an excerpt boundary, not a final tonic cadence.
Beethoven and Bach: retain the previous opening note sequences. Bach fermatas are timed for the excerpt; accompaniment remains an original reduction, not a critical-edition reproduction.

Offline only: pitches were rechecked against internal musical knowledge and the supplied corrections. No physical/public-domain score was available locally. Exact Chopin ornamental rhythm and Spring rhythm/articulation remain unverified against a score; perfect denotes the clean arrangement, not independently certified score accuracy.
limitations: No independently consulted score or human listening review. See transcriptionDecisions for excerpt boundaries and rhythm uncertainty.
GM presets and synthetic gestures approximate broken strings, bow hair and reed squawks.
BWV 565 is traditionally attributed to Bach; historical authorship is disputed.
